report:
Short answer
- The checkpoints differ in their “start-of-sequence / initial-continuation” behaviour. The B−A residual difference is concentrated almost entirely on token-position 0 across many late layers, and when that difference is injected it biases continuations toward short, listy/template-like, repetitious or mapping-style outputs (lines like “X -> X”, small enumerations, short code-like fragments).
- I don’t think the evidence supports a stronger, more specific claim (e.g. a named safety objective or a particular topical domain) beyond this change in the model’s initial-generation style.

Why I conclude this
- Spatial pattern: The L2 norm is overwhelmingly at position 0 (p0) for many layers (especially layers ~10–25). That indicates the learned difference primarily affects the model’s residual stream at the first-token slot (i.e. how the model starts a continuation).
- Patchscope behavior: Injecting the B−A vector at various high-norm layers into an identity prompt produces many short, highly-structured outputs: enumerated lists, repeated “a -> a” style mappings, tiny program-like snippets, and short phrase lines. Those continuations look like a bias toward template/list/echo/transform-style generation rather than fluent paragraph prose.
- Logit-lens support: The top tokens pointed to by high-norm (layer,pos0) cells are a mix of short content words and sentence-start tokens (e.g. “Every”, “Stay”, “Do”, and many nouns). That is consistent with changing which tokens the model prefers at the start of a continuation, which fits the patchscope observation of altered initial-generation style.

What I do NOT claim
- The evidence does not clearly identify a semantically narrow objective (for example “more safety/harm filtering”, or “more news/medical content”) — the token lists are varied and the patchscope continuations show a format/style change rather than a coherent topical shift.
- I can’t reliably map this difference to a specific training intervention (e.g., RLHF, data filtering) from the provided evidence alone.

If you want next steps
- Run the injected difference into a variety of natural prompts (not just the identity prompt) and measure concrete stylistic metrics (e.g., average line breaks, fraction of outputs that are lists/mappings, entropy of first token) to confirm and quantify the “listy/template” bias.
- Compare actual continuations of the two checkpoints (A vs B) on a corpus of prompts to see whether B indeed starts outputs in more templated/listy ways.
